item.description:

item.title: UK social media ban expansion for under-16s could cover YouTube Kids
item.description:
Online age verification champions are a bit like horror movie villains. Once Michael Myers gets inside a house, he's not going to stop with just one or seven kills. He's going to keep killing until you push him out a window, run him over with a car, and throw his body in a lake (and even then, he'll be back again someday). Likewise, once authorities learn that the public and the courts will stand for one form of age verification—say, asking porn platforms to verify user identities—they're suddenly off on a surveillance spree that won't stop until the whole internet is covered. item.title: Open Thread
item.description:
E ight years ago, Democrats harnessed popular anger at Donald Trump to take control of the House. Promising to curb the administration’s excesses, they issued a pile of subpoenas and held Cabinet members in contempt. Rashida Tlaib of Michigan famously vowed to “impeach the motherfucker.” They tried that, twice. In the end, many congressional Democrats concluded, the exercise only hardened partisan allegiances and handed Trump a foil to run against in 2020 and again in 2024. Democrats think this time will be different. It’s not just that their margin in last week’s midterms was bigger, but that economic discontent lets them tie their investigations to their promise to address the cost of living.
